Welcome, Our Dearest Guests

A note before the details — please read this first.

Welcome to our New Year's Eve wedding — black tie, champagne, and a countdown you will never forget. Thank you for choosing to spend the last night of the year with us, in the city that never sleeps.

Everything you need is on this page: times, addresses, where to stay, what to wear, and the RSVP at the bottom. If anything is unclear, message us. We would rather answer twice than have you guess once.

— Isabella & Alexander

Venue, Travel & Stay

Flying in? Start here, then pick a hotel that fits your budget.

The Venue

The Deco Palace, New York — our recommended base if you want one place for the whole celebration.

Open in Google Maps →

Getting Here

John F. Kennedy Airport (JFK) is the nearest airport. Allow about 45–60 minutes by car to Manhattan in normal traffic — book your ride in advance for the main evening.

Parking & Shuttle

Parking is available at the venue where noted in the FAQ. There is no arranged shuttle between hotels, so please plan a ride for each evening and pre-book for late returns.

Where to Stay

Price bands are indicative for planning only — please confirm live rates when you book.

Budget — Midtown guesthouses & innsIndicative band: lower nightly rates. Simple Midtown stays; allow a taxi ride to the palace.
Mid-range — Deco District HotelIndicative band: mid nightly rates. A ten-minute taxi from The Deco Palace, with a late bar.
Premium — The Deco Palace (venue hotel)Indicative band: higher nightly rates. Stay where the party is — no travel on New Year's Eve, the easiest choice of the night.

Travelling with children or elderly family? Tell us in the RSVP message and we will help you choose the most comfortable option.

◆ ◆ ◆

Our Story

How we met, and how we got here — in four moments.

2019 — A Jazz Club

We met between sets

Isabella was singing with the band; Alexander was the only one in the room who knew the second verse. He sang it, quietly, from his table. She noticed. The band noticed too.

2020–2024 — The City Habit

Midnights in Manhattan

Every free evening became the city — jazz clubs, late dinners, and walks home at 2 AM. Alexander plans; Isabella improvises. The habit never stopped.

December 2026 — On New Year's Eve

He asked at midnight

Exactly a year before this wedding, as the city counted down, Alexander asked properly, ring in a velvet box, fireworks over the river. Isabella said yes at twelve-oh-one.

31 December 2027 — Today, With You

Now we want you in the room

Black tie, champagne, and a countdown shared with the people who made us who we are. That is the whole plan — and the only thing missing is you.

Dress Code

Black tie, strictly: gowns or tuxedos, gold accents welcome. Please avoid casual wear entirely — this is a palace on New Year's Eve, and the dress code is part of the celebration.

Black — required
Champagne gold — aim for this
Ivory — welcome
Deep red — welcome

A Note on Gifts

Your presence is the gift — truly. If you still wish to give, a contribution towards our honeymoon is welcome, and we will share details personally with anyone who asks. There is no online registry or payment link on this page, by design.

Questions, Answered

Tap a question to open it.

Children are welcome at the brunch, but the New Year's Eve gala itself is adults-only, so parents can dance until midnight. Please tell us in the RSVP if this changes your plans.

Only if your invitation names a plus-one, or you have confirmed one with us directly. If unsure, write it in the RSVP message and we will confirm — seating is planned by name.

Valet parking is available at The Deco Palace. On New Year's Eve, taxis are scarce after midnight — please pre-book your ride home, or stay at the venue hotel.

Black tie, strictly. Gowns or tuxedos; gold accents welcome. No casual wear, no trainers — the palace dress code is enforced at the door.

No gift is expected — your presence is the gift. If you wish to give, a honeymoon contribution is welcome; ask us personally for details.

December in New York is cold — the palace is fully indoors and heated, but the walk from taxi to door is outdoors. Bring a warm coat; the cloakroom is free.
